note.value: 279 FROM THOMAS BRAY IN EDMONTON (MIDDLESEX) TO THE CHURCHWARDENS AND OVERSEERS OF GREAT CHISHALL, 12 March 1788

text.p: To the Church Wardens & Overseers of the Poor of the Parish of Chisel

I am Sorry I should have Occasion to trouble you but Necessity Obliges me, having had the Misfortune of two fits of illness as you may see by the Apothecaries Bills, as well my Wife has been ill some time not able to do anything which has greatly Distressed me, as I never have been any ways troublesome to you for any Relief before, I hope you will be so kind to take it into Consideration, as the Apothecary is so very Pressing upon me for his Money, and it is not on my Power to pay him any without Selling what few things I have which if I should be Obliged to do, I and my Wife must be Obliged to Come to you for Relief, I hope you Gentlemen will be so kind to Advance the Money for the Payment of these Bills, as my Long illness greatly Distressed us, for a support, or I should not have troubled you, be so kind to Order the payment soon as I am greatly Distressed on Account of it, I am

note.value: 280 FROM THOMAS MORSE IN (GREAT) COGGESHALL TO THE CHURCHWARDENS AND OVERSEERS OF ST JOHN BAPTIST, HEREFORD, 12 MARCH 1750

text.p: This with my humble Service returning many thanks for all favours: to Inform you that the Overseers &c of the Parish have been with me and desired I would write to You forthwith relating to the Money which they Disbusted to me and which I have Recevd from their hands though since the Receiving of Your letter have been Obliged to Shift without - through the Goodness of some Friends and of my Son who has been a Servant here and is out of his time But the Gentlemen have given me Notice that Unless their letters be answered to their Satisfaction within 14 days they will get an Order & bring me home and as I am settled here & through the Help of Some friends Capable of getting my Bread better than if I should come home and as you must be Sensible it will be a great Expense for two People so far advanced in Years to Come so far I hope you will therefore take it into Consideration and so Order the matter that wee may be Continued where we are which will Greatly Oblige Gentleman Your
I should be glad to Receive your answer please to Direct for me the Bull In Coggeshall Essex

note.value: 281 FROM JANE CROSS IN CANTERBURY TO AUSTIN VAILANT, CHURCHWARDEN OF ST BOTOLPH, COLCHESTER, 24 APRIL 1755

text.p:
To you Gentlemen church wardens of the Parish of buttle to whom I happily belong do I now make bold to write being your your poor yet humble Petitioner and first I beg leave to acquaint you I Got safe to cantubery and was loveingly received by my dear mother who was doubtless Glad to see me and is very willing to help me in what is in her power but her acent years makes it not in her power to do Greatly for me neither do I of my self desire to be incombant on my dear mother but desire to labour for my self and my child but its not in my power to subsist with my own labour I therefore appeal to your dear Goodness to consider my case and be please to allow me some small allowance to help bring up my dear baby - my mother is willing to Give me a bed and some sl small trifle to help furnish me a room but I can not except of it till I do receive your kind answer because I can not undertake to pay house rent and maintain my self and child therefore I beg Gentlemen you please to consider it and soon to send me your answer and I hope you will not deny me so small a subsistence as six pence a week which to be sure is but a trifle and my hands must labour hard to do the rest beside Gentlemen you very well know I cam away very bear in apparel and my child like wise and its favouring your charge Greatly that I am come and if you please to consider me in this favour I nor my baby shall never more be a trouble to you but if you deny it me and refuse to help me I must send my child down to you for its for him I desire an allowance as to my self I will work freely and like my own place of abode very well and think to stay hear so long as my dear mother lives but my child I must part from to you if you don't allow me so be please to answer my letter speedily if you please and let me know what you do intend for me I beg the money quarterly and as I came bear and had work to seek I hope you will send me a half a Geney for this quarter mittsumer and I beg you please to send it me by the Colchester hies and leave it at the bear and wheat Sheaf in thames street in london for mr Tallbutt hyeman to cantubery - as if you send a letter be please to direct your letter for me Jane cross at mr bangges in
hospital I lane in st milldreds in cantubery - and pray send with speed I beg - and you will much oblige your humble petitioner and parishsoner

note.value: 593 FROM ANN GARNER (IN ATTLEBOROUGH, NORFOLK) TO MR COOK IN HAVERING-ATTE-BOWER (16 APRIL 1795)

text.p: Ann Garner the wife of James Garner Could wish to be hapy to Live with my husband again but I am very uneasy & unhappy that he have Left me a Gain for I have been Lawful married to him 27 years and have had thirteen Children by him now I think It tic a unjust thing for you Gentleman & officers to harbour married men thear from thear wife and familys now I understand the Letter which mr Cook sent to the Attlburg officer that he have a wife and family in your place and if he be thear I men to be thear my self and beg of you to send me a Answer weather he be thear or near for I think tic not proper for a another woman to in joy my Right his Daught which Laid in when he was thear have Laid il so to hart that thea think she out Live

note.value: 645 FROM MARY PAVETT IN RAINHAM TO HENRY PAVETT IN STRATFORD (ESSEX), (2) MARCH 1748

text.p: Loving Brother This Coms to Let you Now that My husband Died Yesterday and Desire to Now if you Will Com Down and See him Berried for he Life in asad Conditon I desire to Now if you and your Brother Will Be at the Expense of Bearing him if Not to go to the parish and acquaint them of it pray Send apuntal anser By the Barer of What is to be Don in the afaire for Ihave Not got Where With to Defray the Expense of Bering him for if the parish Berries him I must be forced to Com Com to ham parish and With What things I have got I can Make Shift Just to Live and if ham parish Will is to be at the Charge Desire them to Send a note from their hands but I shall be glad if you Will Com Down for their is Somthings that Will be of Servis to you in your Way of Business he Came home of the Saturday Night and Died amonday Noon he Not got acoffin Nor I have got No Money So pray Send Me Word by the Barer from your Loving

note.value: 645A HENRY PAVETT'S ANSWER TO LETTER 645 DATED 2 MARCH (1748)

text.p: Sister I Recved your Leater I am Sorry to her my Brother is dead I heave Ben with the Chorchworden and thay well not Bary him without Ranom Can find a setefiteket from there hands Rainom Praish must Beary him my Brother John and I Cant a ford to Beary him And the Parish must Where he did I Cant no Wais Come Down to See him Beared So my Love to you

note.value: 705 FROM MARY HOWE TO MR RANKING IN COOPERSALE (THEYDON GARNON), 13 JANUARY 1731

text.p: Mr ranking this is to let you know that the doxtor have done what he can for me but my eyes are never the better but rather worse i am to be discharged next wandsday i hope you will be so kind as to send me word how i must come home by next wandsday morning so with humble service to you and your good wife
sir I hope you will exquese me in wrighting of a letter but i did not know no other way So i rest your humble servant

note.value: 706 FROM MARY MARSHALL TO THE CHURCHWARDENS AND OVERSEERS OF THEYDON GARNON, 1 SEPTEMBER 1736

text.p: I am very sorry I am forced to be so troublesome you were so good as to give me one Guinea which I was forced to lay out I have sent word of every penrey at the Bottom I must beg your Godnesses to send me one half Guinea more and I hope that God will bless me and in able me to geet my bread without being troublesome any more I was forced to geet a small malter for bread of my Landlady for without I cant geet my bread I beg you will please to send it me as I may go to work from your poor parishner
they are very urgent for a Certificate

note.value: 708 FROM WIDOW CAMP IN WIDFORD (ESSEX) TO MR HUMERSON IN COOPERSALE (THEYDON GARNON), 12 JULY 1759

text.p: Jam very Sorry that Jam Obliged to write to you for Some Relief but Can no ways help it I have been very Ill a Long time and Obliged to have a Doctor to attend me which hath brought me to Great Nescesity which Ihope you will Consider me Something for it is very Hard with me at present and by doing this I Shall Ever be bound to pray for you Ishould not have sent to you only being too Hard Drove
From your Distressed Humble Sert to Command

note.value: 715 FROM GEORGE OLIVER TO MR LONG, OVERSEER OF WEST THURROCK (1770)

text.p: Mr Long Overseer Sir I hope the gentleman will take it in consideration to allow me something a week for my family the gentleman you have got a family and you must now than a little how to keep a family I have been ill fourteen weeks and I aint had only ten shillings of you and haw do you thing I must keep my family so I have three shillings a week to pay house rent I never trouble you for any think when I am weell It aint my wish now If i could help it there is six of us in family there is nare a one of them able to bring any thing in I cant set here and see my family want when I am close to my own parish I hope in a little while I shall be able to come out again and then I shant want to trouble you gentleman no more I thank you sir to send me an answer

note.value: 747 FROM ANN CLARK IN (BERMONDSEY, LONDON) TO THE REVD DR CHAMBERS IN LITTLE WALTHAM, 9 OCTOBER 1768

text.p: To the woshabel gestes of the paresh the Humble Purtision of ann clark setting forth my grant distress Showing I pade five pound at the indey house to git Him of he after words indeverd to work at abrookous But got ahurt in his leg which was histeth and left me and my family in the greatest distress of your Goodness will bee pleased to send me sum relefe so That with industry imay bee able to git my bread or Else must bee oblige to com don and my family upon The paresh I beige your goodness will take it in to consideration and send me some reelefe as soon as you Reeceive this my husband being deed and weeks Ans his sickness and burel has drove me to the Greatest destrees in complying with this your Poor purtisinor will bee in duty ever bound To pray for you ihad a letter from scotland

And informs me that All my friends their is Ded which mad me not Go on my journey so made no yous of my pas Ps plees to Derect For me to bee Left at the son in wit street near sant gorges church in the Boorow - Sourthwork Pray send an answer By the next post

note.value: 748 FROM TIMOTHY WOODWARD TO MR DRAKE IN WANSTEAD, 1766

text.p: I make bold to trouble you to let you know that Mr Mold who is the master of the house where I am Denies me the liberty of a person going with me to Doctor Taylor twice a week he has told me Downright that I shall go no more I humbly beg of you to be so kind as to think of some way or other to help me at this time for I find myself much better then when I came & it will be a great pity for me to lose this opportunity that you have been so kind as to give me under the blessing of God whereby I may have my sight restored ---- th
sir in so doing you will oblige your Humble servant
